claim: In Fleischner 2017, for solid nodules: when 6–8 mm, one follow-up CT at 6–12 months, with a second scan at 18–24 months for selected cases.
In Fleischner 2017, for subsolid nodules: follow-up at 6–12 months and then periodic surveillance for up to 5 years.
In Fleischner 2017, for solid or subsolid nodules: when smaller than 6 mm in a low-risk patient, no follow-up is generally recommended.
In Fleischner 2017, for solid nodules: when larger than 8 mm, consider CT at 3 months, PET-CT or tissue sampling.
In Fleischner 2017, for nodules under 6 mm in a high-risk patient: an optional CT at 12 months.
In Fleischner 2017, for transient subsolid nodules: the follow-up CT interval is 12 months rather than 3 months.
In Fleischner 2017, for solid nodules: when 6–8 mm, one follow-up CT at 3–6 months.
In Fleischner 2017, for subsolid nodules: periodic surveillance for up to 2 years.
In Fleischner 2017, for subsolid nodules: when 6–8 mm, one follow-up CT at 6–12 months, with a second scan at 18–24 months for selected cases.
In Fleischner 2017, for solid nodules: follow-up at 6–12 months and then periodic surveillance for up to 5 years.
In Bosniak 2019, for solid nodules: when 6–8 mm, one follow-up CT at 6–12 months.
In Fleischner 2017, for perifissural nodules larger than 10 mm: CT at 3 months.
In Fleischner 2017, for nodules under 6 mm in a low-risk patient: an optional CT at 12 months.
In ESE adrenal incidentaloma 2023, for imaging assessment: homogeneous lesions with ≤10 HU on unenhanced CT are benign and do not require any additional imaging, independent of size.
In ESE adrenal incidentaloma 2023, for homogeneous tumours under 4 cm with 11 to 20 HU: immediate additional imaging is recommended.
In ESE adrenal incidentaloma 2023, for lesions over 4 cm that are inhomogeneous or have HU above 20: surgery is usually the management of choice.
In ESE adrenal incidentaloma 2023, for imaging assessment: homogeneous lesions with ≤20 HU on unenhanced CT are benign and need no further imaging.
In ESE adrenal incidentaloma 2023, follow-up at 3 to 6 months after the initial imaging, continuing for 1 to 2 years regardless of imaging features.
In ESE adrenal incidentaloma 2023, for indeterminate lesions: interval imaging at 6 to 12 months is preferred over immediate additional imaging.
In Bosniak 2019, for class IIF: follow-up imaging at 6 months, 12 months, then annually for 5 years.
In Bosniak 2019: the update incorporates MRI and establishes definitions for previously vague imaging terms.

In Fleischner 2017, rule for solid nodules: under 6 mm in low-risk patients no routine follow-up; 6–8 mm CT at 6–12 months then 18–24 months in selected cases; over 8 mm CT at 3 months, PET-CT or tissue sampling.
In Fleischner 2017, rule for solid nodules: under 6 mm in low-risk patients no routine follow-up; 6–8 mm CT at 3–6 months; over 8 mm CT at 3 months, PET-CT or tissue sampling.
In Fleischner 2017, rule for subsolid nodules: under 6 mm no follow-up; 6–8 mm one CT at 6–12 months and a second at 18–24 months; over 8 mm CT at 3 months, PET-CT or tissue sampling.
